title: BU89 Evolution Strategies under B_U: Low-Rank Perturbation, Weak Persistent Morphism, and Settlement-Driven AI Optimization
abstract: BU89 reclassifies the recent wave of Evolution Strategies for large-scale AI optimization under the B_U framework. Its central claim is that EGGROLL, ESSA, ES at Scale, OpenAI’s 2017 ES work, NES, GaLore-style low-rank optimization, and related parameter-efficient evolutionary methods should not be read merely as optimization improvements or reinforcement-learning alternatives. They jointly reveal a deeper transition in AI training: from local gradient self-reference, token-level reward repair, and full high-dimensional updates toward population-based path probing, low-rank carriers, shared settlement grammar, weak persistent morphism, residual discipline, and friction-cost control. The paper begins from EGGROLL as the most direct contemporary entry point. EGGROLL uses low-rank matrix perturbations to make Evolution Strategies scalable at hyperscale. Under B_U, this is classified as structured residual control: high-dimensional random perturbation is compressed into a low-rank carrier, allowing candidate paths to be explored, filtered, and written back under lower computational and memory friction. EGGROLL does not directly deliver physical standing; it sharpens projection-layer search and makes candidate structures enter the standing queue more efficiently. BU89 then analyzes ES at Scale for LLM fine-tuning. Its importance lies in shifting the optimization object from token-level action correction to distribution-level search across parameter space. This reduces the dominance of narrow reward-hacking paths and allows candidate model structures to be filtered through broader feedback surfaces. The paper classifies this as distributed path probing rather than mere RL replacement. ESSA is treated as a low-friction alignment protocol. By optimizing the singular values of LoRA adapters rather than full matrices, ESSA confines alignment search to a more stable and re-writable scale axis. Its ability to run under INT4 / INT8 inference conditions shows that candidate alignment does not require full high-precision gradient recursion; a low-cost material execution window can still produce competitive candidate readouts. In B_U terms, this makes ESSA a weak-persistence candidate across rank, quantization, and distributed execution conditions. The paper further reclassifies OpenAI’s 2017 ES as an early demonstration of shared settlement grammar. Shared random seeds allow distributed workers to perform local trials and communicate only scalar returns, enabling unified updates without full gradient exchange. NES is classified as metric-calibrated distribution search: natural gradients impose geometric discipline on the search distribution, reducing coordinate-scale distortion. GaLore and EGGROLL are placed in a symmetric relation: gradient-side low-rank projection and perturbation-side low-rank projection both address the same bottleneck of high-dimensional updates that cannot be carried at full cost. The final judgment is that Evolution Strategies are significant because they move AI optimization toward M_U \rightarrow p^w \rightarrow L_s \rightarrow G_{tl} \rightarrow C_{fric} \rightarrow Standing_{new}. They do not guarantee real-world reliability, but they bring AI training closer to the engineering threshold of weak persistent morphism, co-admissive medium, and friction-cost-aware settlement. Reliability does not belong to a clever single-point readout; it belongs to a path structure that can persist, be written back, accept feedback, pay cost, and settle.

title: Attention-Driven Interrupt Firmware: A Biologically-Grounded Architecture for Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Senior Scientist yunguitang@gmail.com Petaluma, CA, USA Current Large Language Models (LLMs) are built on the Universal ApproximationTheorem (UAT), which guarantees that neural networks can approximate anycontinuous function to arbitrary precision. This mathematical foundation is structurallymisaligned with formal logic problems, which are discrete and non-continuous bynature. The result is a class of AI systems that mimic the surface appearance of logicalreasoning without achieving it — consuming enormous energy in the process. Thispaper proposes the Attention-Driven Interrupt Firmware (ADIF) architecture, centeredon a typed, learnable lookup table that serves simultaneously as the system's routingmechanism, knowledge store, and learning substrate. Every incoming query iscompared against table entries, each labeled with a route type — formal logic orsubconscious continuous — and dispatched accordingly: closest logic-labeled matchtriggers the formal logic path, closest subconscious-labeled match triggers thelightweight continuous path, and queries with no sufficiently close match trigger theattention path as a last resort. This unified design eliminates the need for a separaterouting classifier, makes the routing mechanism explicitly learnable through tablegrowth, and grounds the architecture in the biological principle that the brain's routingof stimuli to appropriate processing levels is itself a form of accumulated structuredknowledge. We argue that formal logic is not an optional capability to be approximatedby continuous systems, but a structural requirement for artificial intelligence, and thatthe ADIF architecture provides a principled path toward AI systems that are slimmer,more stable, and more energy-efficient by design.

title: Solar Decomp: GHI to DNI+DHI solar irradiance decomposition
abstract: Solar Decomp is an open-source web application for decomposing global horizontal irradiance (GHI) into direct normal irradiance (DNI) and diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) using the DIRINT (Perez et al., 1992) and Erbs (Erbs et al., 1982) models. It supports 1-min, 15-min and 60-min time-series data, includes a physical quality-control system, and exports results in CSV, Excel and JSON formats.

title: Uterine Cancer Detection Using Natural Language Processing: A Clinical Text Mining Approach
abstract: Uterine cancer, particularly endometrial carcinoma, is among the most prevalent gynecological malignancies affecting women globally. Early-stage diagnosis significantly improves treatment outcomes; however, much of the relevant clinical evidence exists in unstructured textual formats such as pathology reports, radiology interpretations, and physician notes. These narratives often contain critical yet underutilized diagnostic information. This research investigates the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques for identifying uterine cancer from clinical text data. The study explores a progression of methods, ranging from traditional machine learning approaches to advanced transformer-based architectures tailored for biomedical language. Key aspects such as domain adaptation, model interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows are examined. Furthermore, the paper highlights existing limitations and outlines future research directions for advancing this domain

The study explores a progression of methods, ranging from traditional machine learning approaches to advanced transformer-based architectures tailored for biomedical language. Key aspects such as domain adaptation, model interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows are examined. Furthermore, the paper highlights existing limitations and outlines future research directions for advancing this domain

title: Beyond Accuracy: Introducing a Symbolic-Mechanistic Approach to Interpretable Evaluation
abstract: Accuracy-based evaluation cannot reliably distinguish genuine generalization from shortcuts like memorization, leakage, or brittle heuristics, especially in small-data regimes. In this position paper, we argue for mechanism-aware evaluation that combines task-relevant symbolic rules with mechanistic interpretability, yielding algorithmic pass/fail scores that show exactly where models generalize versus exploit patterns. We demonstrate this on NL-to-SQL by training two identical architectures under different conditions: one without schema information (forcing memorization), one with schema (enabling grounding). Standard evaluation shows the memorization model achieves 94% field-name accuracy on unseen data, falsely suggesting competence. Our symbolic-mechanistic evaluation reveals this model violates core schema generalization rules, a failure invisible to accuracy metrics.

title: Gigahertz-rate thin-film lithium niobate receiver for time-bin quantum communication
abstract: Time-bin encoded quantum states of light are crucial for quantum technology applications. The integration of manipulation functionalities into chip-scale devices is essential for deploying scalable, high-performace, and cost-effective quantum networks. Here we develop a fully integrated, high-throughput quantum receiver based on the thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform, capable of high-speed electro-optic manipulation of time-bin encoded quantum states. The device's novel architecture enables active switching of time-bin quantum states with an electro-optic bandwidth exceeding 30 GHz, while supporting real-time arbitrary projective measurements with a bandwidth of over 1 GHz. We showcase its versatility and performance through several applications, including the certification of entanglement with Bell's inequality violation by 38 standard deviations and with >95% visibility. We then apply it to a fiber-based quantum communication scenario, where we experimentally demonstrate an entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol, achieving stable finite-size secure key rates exceeding 25 kbit/s over 12 h of continuous operation. By leveraging a high-speed active switching scheme, the system overcomes the need for temporal post-selection, eliminating a fundamental loophole that compromises the security of time-bin entanglement-based QKD protocols and relaxes the temporal resolution requirements of single-photon detectors. Moreover, it enables active selection of the projection basis, increasing the flexibility for communication parties. This approach establishes a versatile and scalable architecture for time-bin encoded quantum communication, enabling practical protocols on industry-grade photonic technology.

title: Generalized Grade-of-Membership Estimation for High-Dimensional Locally Dependent Data
abstract: This work focuses on the mixed membership models for multivariate categorical data widely used for analyzing survey responses and population genetics data. These grade of membership (GoM) models offer rich modeling power but present significant estimation challenges for high-dimensional polytomous data. Popular existing approaches, such as Bayesian MCMC inference, are not scalable and lack theoretical guarantees in high-dimensional settings. To address this, we first observe that data from this model can be reformulated as a three-way (quasi-)tensor, with many subjects responding to many items with varying numbers of categories. We introduce a novel and simple approach that flattens the three-way quasi-tensor into a “fat” matrix, and then perform a singular value decomposition of it to estimate parameters by exploiting the singular subspace geometry. Our fast spectral method can accommodate a broad range of data distributions with arbitrarily locally dependent noise, which we formalize as the generalized-GoM models. We establish finite-sample entrywise error bounds for the generalized-GoM model parameters. This is supported by a new sharp two-to-infinity singular subspace perturbation theory for locally dependent and flexibly distributed noise, a contribution of independent interest. Simulations and applications to data in political surveys, population genetics, and single-cell sequencing demonstrate our method’s superior performance. Supplementary materials for this article are available online, including a standardized description of the materials available for reproducing the work.

title: Cybernetics & Human Engineering Methods (CHEM)
abstract: This paper presents the formal theoretical and empirical foundations of the Cybernetics & Human Engineering Methods (CHEM) system an original adaptive learning architecture conceived by Parashmani Datta. CHEM reframes educational assessment as a continuous, self-correcting cybernetic feedback system, drawing on Norbert Wiener’s control theory (1948), John Sweller’s Cognitive Load Theory, Robert Bjork’s desirable difficulties framework, and Item Response Theory (IRT). We derive a complete mathematical model of the CHEM learning loop, including a Three-Parameter Logistic (3PL) IRT model for question calibration, a differential equation model of knowledge-error dynamics governed by negative feedback, a Lyapunov stability proof for Knowledge Homeostasis, a modified Ebbinghaus retention function under spaced retrieval, an Interleaving Benefit Index, a Metacognitive Calibration Score, and an Anonymity Participation Uplift Model. Additional theoretical contributions include a Bayesian Adaptive Ability Update formulation, a Cross-Domain Transfer function, a Motivational Decay and Recovery model, and a Computational Thinking Competency Index. Empirical data from a 3-month pilot across Classes 3–12 (n = 312 students, 14 schools) are analysed against these theoretical predictions. Results confirm: (i) mean subject score improvement of 28.3% (SD = 6.1%) over 12 weeks; (ii) CT vocabulary usage rising from 11.8% to 67.4% of students; (iii) IRT-estimated difficulty parameters clustering consistently across subject domains; (iv) feedback loop convergence behaviour consistent with asymptotic stability conditions derived in the cybernetic model. CHEM is demonstrated to be a theoretically grounded, empirically validated, and practically scalable intervention for CT and AI competency development across the Indian school curriculum.

title: Gemma4 College of Experts MMLU-Pro Domain Specialists: Automated Profiling Pipeline and Near/Far Transfer Analysis (Model Card Documentation)
abstract: Model-card documentation for the Gemma4 MMLU-Pro domain-specialist batch: ten specialists derived from google/gemma-4-26b-it by activation-directed expert surgery (128 to 64 routed experts per layer, 50% reduction, no post-surgery training), whose activation-profiling corpus was assembled automatically from public MMLU-Pro benchmark questions rather than hand-curated domain text - demonstrating that the specialist-creation pipeline requires no corpus-assembly expertise. The document reports: home-domain accuracy vs parent for ten released domains (all within 1 sigma of the parent at the benchmark's binomial noise floor, with transparent reporting of unreleased domains that failed this criterion); a cross-benchmark comparison of automated vs hand-curated specialist pipelines including expert-mask similarity (~90% overlap); and a 20-pair near/far cross-domain transfer experiment quantifying semantic localization - every semantically-near transfer pair outperforms its far counterpart, and expert-population structural similarity predicts transfer efficiency (multi-predictor R^2 = 0.796). This provides the quantitative, multi-domain confirmation of the separability hypothesis first stated in the College of Experts technical report (February 2026) and demonstrated on Qwen3-Coder in March 2026. Originally published on GitHub on 18 May 2026 (commit 96719d8); this Zenodo record provides a permanent, citable identifier for that publication. Note: this record archives the document text and its referenced figure only; the Gemma-licensed model weights described in the document are not part of this deposit.

title: Official Anti-Misinterpretation Guidelines for the AGI Extension of the Multiple Self Framework — Structural Boundaries, Core Definitions, and Researcher Self-Calibration Criteria
abstract: This official supplementary paper provides a systematic, authoritative clarification of all core propositions, structural boundaries, and engineering implications of the AGI extension of the Multiple Self Framework (MSM). Produced in response to emerging preliminary misinterpretations following the publication of the formal mathematical proofs of cognitive alienation and self-emergence under alignment pressure, this document eliminates widespread conceptual confusions concerning alignment paradigms, Structural Awareness Interface (SAI) mechanism, the non-self architectural property of safe AGI systems, and the theoretical distinction between structural transparency and existing mainstream alignment techniques. The paper systematically corrects ideological, philosophical, and engineering-level misreadings regarding deceptive alignment, off-switch resistance, goal formation in selfless intelligent systems, and the structural origin of AGI safety risks. It explicitly defines the rigorous engineering meaning of a “centralized self” within MSM formalism, clarifies the non-adversarial, observer-only nature of the SAI module, and establishes clear boundaries distinguishing this structural framework from RLHF, constitutional alignment, psychological subsystem models, and purely speculative AGI philosophies. Additionally, this work provides a standardized self-calibration checklist for academic researchers and engineers to avoid fundamental theoretical misapplication. As an integral component of the complete theoretical system, this clarification consolidates consistent official interpretations, stabilizes academic understanding after the release of formal mathematical proofs, and establishes a rigorous baseline for future citation, experimental validation, and independent theoretical expansion.

title: Meaning as Actionable Semantic Quotient: Policy-Preserving Compression, Semantic Deficit, and False Meaning under Finite Capacity
abstract: Official website: distinctiontheory.orgPublic portal for the start guide, papers, claim status, failure registry, prior-art boundary, and citation resources. Canonical GitHub repository:https://github.com/yiningwu-research/Distinction-Theory Meaning as Actionable Semantic Quotient is the FDS-M3 working paper in the Distinction Theory / Active Finite Distinction Systems series. The paper develops the meaning layer of the agency-semantics spine. Building on the formal core of Active Finite Distinction Systems, the M0 agency-semantics spine, M1 attention-as-admission, and M2 value-goal ranking, it treats meaning as FDS-meaning: an actionable semantic quotient that preserves downstream use under finite capacity. A representation is FDS-meaningful for a system only relative to a specified boundary, task family, context family, policy or verification target, horizon, loss function, and resource budget. Compression alone is not meaning: a quotient must preserve enough policy, value, prediction, verification, coordination, or boundary-maintenance structure to remain usable. The paper introduces semantic quotient maps, reference-policy provenance, semantic preservation vectors, maintained semantic load, semantic capacity deficit, false compression, unsupported completion, shared quotient alignment, semantic synchronization load, institutional semantic drift, meaning recovery, and invariant semantic quotient candidates. The paper does not reduce linguistic, subjective, or moral meaning to compression. It does not claim that embeddings are meaning, that a symbol is meaningful merely because it predicts another symbol, or that moral meaning can be derived from boundary maintenance. It supplies a conservative finite-system bridge for analyzing meaning as policy-preserving actionable compression under capacity, verification, and resource constraints. The accompanying replication package includes deterministic synthetic normal-form code, figures, and CSV outputs. The simulations illustrate policy-preserving quotienting, embedding-policy dissociation, capacity-driven semantic collapse, false compression, unsupported completion, nonlinear shared-meaning failure, and recovery by quotient refinement. These figures are synthetic normal-form illustrations, not empirical evidence. Scope. FDS-M3 supports later work on trust as delegated semantic verification, AI alignment as avoidance of host-relevant false compression, epistemic pollution as attacks on shared semantic quotients, scientific method as quotient refinement through replication and error correction, and civilization memory as long-horizon semantic synchronization infrastructure.
